title: Invariant measure
description: A double well $\Psi = \frac{(x^2 - 4)^2}{16} + \frac{y^2}{2}$ with σ = 1. The particles start uniformly in a rectangle. The pink fill is the smoothed empirical measure $\hat\rho_h$; the KL window compares it with the Gibbs density $\pi \propto e^{-2\Psi/\sigma^2}$, the stationary solution of the Fokker–Planck equation $\partial_t\rho = \nabla\cdot(\rho\nabla\Psi) + \frac{\sigma^2}{2}\Delta\rho$.

questions.text: Where is $\hat\rho_h$ highest once it has settled, and why there?
The KL curve levels off near the dashed smoothing floor, not at 0. Why?
Lower σ to 0.6. How does the invariant density change, and what does that do to the time KL needs to settle?
